rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / BASICS / CHAPTER 4

slides.title: Functions
slides.main: A function is a named block of code: define it once, call it as often as needed.

items.title: Definition
items.sub: The def keyword, a name, parameters, an indented body

items.title: Call
items.sub: Name plus parentheses: the code runs

items.title: Result
items.sub: Hands back a value and ends the function

body.text: You have already called built-in functions: print, len, type, int. Now we write our own.

slides.title: Definition and call
slides.sub: def defines a function, parentheses run it
slides.main: A definition runs nothing: the code runs only on a call.

body.text:
def hello():
    print("Hello!")

hello()
hello()
hello()
Define a function before calling it, or Python does not know the name.

slides.title: Parameters
slides.sub: A parameter is a name in the definition, an argument is a value at the call
slides.main: One function serves a thousand cases: different arguments, same code.

body.text:
def hello(name):
    print("Hello,", name)

hello("Anya")
hello("Boris")

slides.title: return
slides.sub: Hand the result back to the caller
slides.main: print is for people, return is for programs.

body.text:
def square(x):
    return x * x

result = square(5)
print(result)
print(square(3) + square(4))
No return: the function returns None, that is, “nothing”.

slides.title: Branches and early exit
slides.sub: return ends the function at once
slides.main: On every path of execution, a function must return something.

slides.title: Default values
slides.main: Parameters with defaults come after plain ones; keyword arguments go in any order.

body.text:
def power(x, n=2):
    return x ** n

print(power(5))
print(power(5, 3))
print(power(n=3, x=2))

slides.title: Scope
slides.sub: Local variables live only inside the function
slides.main: Data in through parameters, answer out through return; do not touch outer variables.

body.text:
def f():
    local = 10
    return local

f()
print(local)   # NameError
Assigning inside a function creates a new local variable and leaves the outer one alone.

slides.title: Docstring and names
slides.main: One function, one task; if the description needs “and”, split it.

body.text:
def is_even(n):
    """Return True if n is even."""
    return n % 2 == 0

print(is_even.__doc__)
Return True if n is even.
A name is a verb or a question: count_total, is_even. Not f1 or func.

slides.title: Functions call functions
slides.sub: Decomposition: a big task from small ones
slides.main: A good program reads like a table of contents: each function names its task briefly.

slides.title: Recursion
slides.main: You need a base case, or recursion never stops.

slides.title: assert: checking functions
slides.sub: A claim: true is silent, false is an error
slides.main: Check typical values and edge cases: zero, negatives, the empty string.

body.text:
def square(x):
    return x * x

assert square(3) == 9
assert square(0) == 0
assert square(-2) == 4
print("all good")

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: Most mistakes are caught in a minute by reading the code aloud.

body.text:
def double(x):
    print(x * 2)      # printed, but did not return

r = double(4)
print(r)               # None
print(double)          # no parentheses: the function object itself
Also: call before definition, editing an outer variable, a function that “does too much”.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Data in through parameters, answer out through return.

items.sub: Indented body; a call runs the code

items.title: Result
items.sub: Hands back a value; without it, None
